subject: Vocabulary
description: Vocabulary by Latin roots: PORT (carry, gate) and MIT/MIS (send) — high-yield word families for SSC, IBPS, banking exams.

questions.stem: The word PORTABLE means 'able to be carried'. Which other word shares the root 'PORT' meaning 'carry'?
questions.explanation: Latin root PORT- = 'to carry' (from 'portare'). WORD FAMILY: PORTABLE (can be carried), TRANSPORT (carry across), IMPORT (carry IN), EXPORT (carry OUT), DEPORT (carry away — official banishment), SUPPORT (carry from beneath, hold up), REPORT (carry back), PURPORT (claim to carry, profess), COMPORT (carry oneself, behave), DISPORT (entertain, play). RELATED: 'PORT' as harbour/gate is from a different Latin root 'porta' (gate) — PORTAL, PORTICO, PORTER (gatekeeper). PORTHOLE blends 'port' (gate-opening) + 'hole'. PORTRAIT is from Latin 'protrahere' (to draw forth) — same Latin family but different nuance. PYQ-ANGLE: word-root MCQs require students to disambiguate similar-looking words. INSIGHT: knowing 50-100 Latin/Greek roots gives access to 5,000-10,000 English words via context-deduction — examined heavily in SSC CGL Tier 2 vocab. EXAMINER MINDSET: testing METALINGUISTIC awareness — vocabulary by morphological analysis, not rote memorization.

questions.stem: What does the word DEPORT (root: 'port') most likely mean?

options.option_text: To officially expel from a country

questions.explanation: DEPORT = de- (away from) + port (carry) → 'to carry away/expel'. In legal terms, deportation is the formal removal of a non-citizen from a country, usually for visa violations or criminal offenses. INDIA CONTEXT: under the Foreigners Act 1946, India can deport persons present without valid documents — historically, this includes Bangladeshi/Rohingya migrants in some states. SOUL/CHARACTER MEANING: 'deportment' (= behaviour, conduct) — how one CARRIES oneself. TRIPLE-BARREL: 'deportee' = the person deported; 'deportation' = the act; 'deport' = the verb. RELATED — INTERNATIONAL: ASYLUM is the OPPOSITE of deportation — protected status given to refugees. NOTABLE DEPORTATION CASES: Edward Snowden (US whistleblower) sought asylum to AVOID deportation; Julian Assange (WikiLeaks) extradited from UK to US in 2024-25. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'deport/import/export' appear in SSC vocab + economics PYQs as both root-Q and concept-Q.

questions.stem: What is the meaning of the word TRANSMIT (root: 'mit' = send)?

options.option_text: To send across or pass along
A type of gear in vehicles.

questions.explanation: TRANSMIT = trans- (across) + mit (send) → 'to send across'. MEANING: pass along (signals, diseases, messages, information). EXAMPLES: 'TV signals are transmitted via satellites.' 'Mosquitoes transmit malaria.' 'Genetic traits are transmitted from parents to offspring.' WORD FAMILY (root 'MIT/MIS' = send): TRANSMIT, EMIT (send out), OMIT (leave out, send-away), ADMIT (send-in, accept), REMIT (send back, pay), SUBMIT (send under, yield), COMMIT (send with, pledge), PERMIT (send through, allow), DISMISS (send away). NOTE: MIT becomes MIS in past forms — TRANSMITTED, OMITTED. APPLICATION IN SCIENCE: a TRANSMITTER (radio/TV) sends signals; a RECEIVER picks them up. In medicine: 'sexually transmitted infections' (STIs); 'vector-transmitted diseases' (mosquito-borne). MISSION = 'a task of being sent' (same root). MISSILE = 'a thing sent forth'. PYQ FREQUENCY: 1-2 'mit/mis' words per SSC CGL Tier 2 vocab section.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: To give off or send out
To receive light from a source.
To bounce light off a surface.

questions.explanation: EMIT = e- (out, from Latin ex-) + mit (send) → 'to send out'. Used for radiations, sounds, smells, light, gases. SCIENCE EXAMPLES: 'The bulb EMITS light.' 'Volcanoes EMIT ash and gases.' 'Bees EMIT pheromones.' RELATED FORMS: EMISSION (act of emitting); EMITTER (device/object that emits); CARBON EMISSIONS (a key climate-change topic). INDIA POLICY ANGLE: India announced NET-ZERO target by 2070 at COP26 (Glasgow, 2021); current per-capita CO₂ emissions ~1.9 tonnes (vs world avg ~4.5, US ~16). PHYSICS: emission spectra (each element emits a unique pattern of light) — basis of spectroscopy. WORD-FAMILY MEMORY-TRICK for 'mit' words: EMIT (out), OMIT (off), TRANSMIT (across), ADMIT (in), REMIT (back), COMMIT (with), PERMIT (through), SUBMIT (under). PYQ ANGLE: SSC, IBPS, RBI Grade B all test 'emit/emit-' frequently — also general-awareness Qs on India's climate commitments.

questions.stem: What does the word REMIT mean (root: 'mit' = send)?

options.option_text: To repeat a task again. (option here)
To remove from a list always.

questions.explanation: REMIT = re- (back) + mit (send) → 'to send back'. MOST COMMON USE: send money back (e.g., NRI remittances to India). 'Workers remit ₹50,000 to family every month.' OTHER MEANINGS: (1) FORGIVE — 'remit a debt/sin/punishment' (forgive, cancel). (2) DECREASE — 'symptoms remit' (medical: lessen, abate). (3) REFER — 'remit the case to a lower court' (legal). NOUN — REMITTANCE: money sent back home. INDIA STATS: India is the WORLD'S LARGEST RECIPIENT of remittances — ~$130 billion in 2024-25 (mostly from US, UAE, Saudi Arabia). Kerala receives ~₹1.5 lakh crore annually from Gulf workers. WORLD BANK: remittances to LMICs (Low/Middle Income Countries) reached ~$655 billion in 2023 — exceeding FDI. ECONOMIC IMPACT: India's remittances support ~30 million households, smoothing rural poverty. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'remittances' is a top GK fact for SSC, banking, RBI Grade B. EXAM ANGLE: this Q tests both vocabulary AND general economic awareness.

questions.stem: Which word means 'A formal expulsion that carries away from a place'?
questions.explanation: DEPORTATION = the act of deporting; formal removal of a foreign national from a country. RELATED: 'extradition' is a SIMILAR term but specifically refers to handing a person over to ANOTHER country to face legal proceedings — based on bilateral treaties. INDIA'S EXTRADITION TREATIES: India has treaties with ~50 countries; recent high-profile cases — Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi (extraditions sought from UK), Tahawwur Rana (extradited from US to India in 2025 for Mumbai 26/11 attack involvement). LEGAL FRAMEWORK in India: Foreigners Act 1946, Extradition Act 1962. WORD-CONFUSION: 'reportation' is not a standard English word; 'comportation' is rare/archaic. EXAM-FAVOURITE TRICK: examiners offer plausibly-spelled fakes alongside the correct term. METHOD: think morphology — 'de-port-ation' = 'away-carry-act' = a real English word. PYQ ANGLE: vocabulary + UPSC current-affairs cross-link via extradition.

questions.stem: Which word means 'to give up one's authority and surrender to higher power' (root 'mit' = send)?
questions.explanation: SUBMIT = sub- (under) + mit (send) → 'to send under, yield to'. PRIMARY MEANINGS: (1) YIELD — 'submit to authority' / 'submit to fate'. (2) PRESENT — 'submit a report to the boss' (the more common modern usage). (3) PROPOSE — 'I submit that the witness is unreliable' (legal/formal argument). PSYCHOLOGY: 'dominance vs submission' is a key behavioural axis in many species — wolf packs, primates. ETYMOLOGY: 'submission' originally military — surrendering to a stronger force. CHRISTIAN/ISLAMIC USAGE: Islam literally means 'submission [to God]'; 'Muslim' = 'one who submits'. MEMORY TRICK FOR 'MIT' WORDS: VISUALIZE prefixes as DIRECTIONS — sub (under), com (with), per (through), e (out), trans (across), o (off), re (back), a/ad (toward). EXAM-USEFUL: distinguish 'submit' (yield/send under) from other -mit verbs by prefix-meaning. PYQ ANGLE: SSC CGL Tier 2 vocab section reuses this word-family analysis 1-2× per paper.
